source.title: Adam-family Methods with Decoupled Weight Decay in Deep Learning
source.authors: Kuang-Yu Ding; Nachuan Xiao; Kim-Chuan Toh

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares AdamD with Adam and AdamW on image-classification and language-modeling test performance using a new optimizer. Those results bear conceptually on optimizer and weight-decay conditions in V4, but they do not reproduce the original optimizer comparisons.
record.gate_note: The AdamD/Adam/AdamW training and test curves and language-model perplexity comparisons are the study's own results. The cited optimizer and weight-decay findings in the introduction and discussion are prior work, not rows. The residual plots and theoretical SGD approximation are not direct measurements of the training–test generalization gap described in the versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam with coupled weight decay against AdamW on held-out performance, testing V4's decoupled-weight-decay qualification. Its AdamD results extend that comparison, but no experiment compares adaptive methods with SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate, but the language-model advantage over AdamW is reported across all tested LSTM depths, not only larger LSTMs. AdamD matches Adam for one and two layers and improves test perplexity by at least 2 units for three layers. The authors propose asymptotic SGD tracking as an explanation for generalization; they do not experimentally establish SGD-level performance.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces AdamD and compares it with Adam and AdamW; uses different experiments and does not reproduce the original optimizer-comparison protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model family change the reported optimizer ranking: AdamD is nearly as good as AdamW on image classification; its language-modeling performance is similar to Adam for 1- and 2-layer LSTMs and better for the 3-layer LSTM, while AdamD and Adam are described as better than AdamW overall on language modeling.

fits_no_version.finding: AdamD's auxiliary-sequence residual tends toward zero, supporting the proposed asymptotic approximation to SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, AdamD asymptotically tracks an auxiliary SGD sequence; this does not establish equal held-out performance to SGD.

record.problems: Test metrics are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The prose gives broad comparisons rather than separate outcomes for each image-classification model. The reported experiments compare AdamD with Adam and AdamW; they do not directly compare with SGD or test an optimizer-induced training–test gap.
record.rows_left_out: Training-accuracy and training-loss curves are shown in Figures 1–4 and Figure 6, but are not extracted because the version concerns held-out performance and the plotted results do not provide numerical train–test gaps. Figures 5 reports residual norms, which do not measure the versioned generalization gap.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Adaptive methods versus SGD or momentum SGD; recovery to SGD-level performance; limited versus broader tuning; switching from Adam to SGD. AdamD also changes the momentum schedule, so its advantage does not isolate weight decoupling alone.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: States refer specifically to V4's decoupling qualification. Image results rely on the authors' collective verbal comparison because the supplied text does not preserve readable curve values. The language results qualify the conditional benefit of decoupling rather than challenge V4's adaptive-versus-SGD claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

The paper compares Adam-family methods on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 and Penn Treebank, but does not compare SGD or momentum SGD, test broad versus limited tuning, or isolate the effect of switching optimizers or decoupled weight decay.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.

relationships.condition: ResNet34 and DenseNet121 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, with learning-rate searches and fixed weight decay.
relationships.reason: R1–R4 support the decoupling qualification: the authors report better generalization for AdamW than Adam, with AdamD usually comparable to AdamW; recovery relative to SGD is untested.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW improves generalization over Adam, and AdamD is usually comparable to AdamW. Whether these methods reach SGD's performance is untested.

source_check.condition: ResNet34 and DenseNet121 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, with learning-rate searches and fixed weight decay.
source_check.reason: R1–R4 and Section 6.1.1 support improved generalization with AdamW relative to Adam; SGD parity remains untested.

relationships.condition: One-, two-, and three-layer LSTMs on Penn Treebank.
relationships.reason: R5–R7 show that decoupling through AdamW does not improve performance here: Adam and AdamD generalize better than AdamW, demonstrating dependence on workload and optimizer formulation.
relationships.display_finding: Adam and AdamD generalized better than AdamW at every tested depth, so separating weight decay from the gradient update did not improve these language models.

relation.reason: The study reports its own held-out optimizer comparisons bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: Different experiments directly test V4's decoupled-weight-decay qualification through Adam-versus-AdamW held-out comparisons.

source_check.notes: Absolute metric values and numerical baselines are figure-only; Adam is the qualitative comparator. R7 additionally reports a prose-stated AdamD advantage of at least 2 perplexity units over Adam; asymptotic SGD tracking does not establish SGD-level held-out performance.

statements.correction: PTB LSTMs: Adam and AdamD generalize better than AdamW. AdamD matches Adam for one and two layers; three-layer AdamD test perplexity is at least 2 units below Adam. No experimental SGD comparison. V4 label for this condition group: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The PTB comparison is accurate, but assigning this study to challenges overstates its bearing on V4's qualified remedy. SGD recovery is untested.
